newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission delays energy taxation revision.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission delays energy taxation revision.

text.p: The European Commission delayed on Wednesday plans to increase and extend EU-wide, minimum tax rates for petrol and diesel fuels, spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas told a news conference on Wednesday.
"It did not adopt the decision today. It will do it at a subsequent occasion once Mr Monti has finalised the text," van der Pas said.
Mario Monti, the European Commissioner responsible for the EU internal market, had hoped to present the plans to a meeting of European economic and finance ministers next Monday.

The proposal would increase EU-wide minimum excise duties on motor and heating fuels and introduce a minimum tax on electricity, natural gas and coal, which are not currently covered by EU rules. For most products the levels would be below the rates currently levied in the 15-nation bloc.

It comes in the wake of years of fruitless negotiations over the introduction of an EU carbon tax, backed by the Commission and some countries as a way to tackle rising carbon dioxide emissions from burning fossil fuels but rejected by others as interference in national tax-raising powers.

"There's clearly a general recognition that we must advance," van der Pas said of Commissioners' remarks in their regular weekly meeting. He said that any eventual proposal would have to be fiscally neutral, meaning that it would not increase a country's overall tax burden.

One way to achieve this would be for an informal balance matching energy tax increases with cuts in employment taxes, something the Commission has to tread very carefully around both because of political sensitivity about budgets as capitals prepare for economic and monetary union and the fact that the Commission has no jurisdiction on national income tax level.
"There is no question that the Commission will go into that area (labour taxation). It goes without saying that there, it's a question of member state responsibility," he said.
Van der Pas was unable to predict when Monti would produce his revised proposal, saying only that the Commissioner wanted "to proceed quickly". -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
